CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the ongoing treatment for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on symptom management and medication efficacy since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a slight improvement in his overall well-being since the last visit. He notes that his anxiety remains relatively stable; however, the irritability persists, particularly in high-pressure work situations. Mr. Smith has continued to adhere to his sertraline regimen of 300 mg daily, and while he acknowledges some improvement in his mood variability, he still experiences challenges with concentration, particularly during meetings.
His tension-type headaches have remained stable, occurring approximately once a week with an intensity of 3 to 4 out of 10. He reports that the topiramate at 150 mg daily has been effective, and he has reduced his ibuprofen usage to once a month for breakthrough headaches. Mr. Smith continues to report improved sleep quality, averaging 7 to 8 hours per night, which he attributes to the combination of trazodone and melatonin. However, he still experiences occasional morning grogginess, which he finds concerning.
Despite the improvements in sleep and headache management, Mr. Smith describes ongoing fatigue, particularly in the afternoons, which he attributes to his demanding work schedule. He expresses a desire to explore additional strategies to enhance his energy levels and overall productivity.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (reduced frequency) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (discontinued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in regular physical activity, including brisk walks and weekend hikes. He has maintained a balanced diet and further reduced his caffeine intake, which he believes has positively impacted his anxiety levels. His mindfulness practices remain a vital component of his daily routine, and he reports that meditation and yoga have become integral in managing stress. He also continues his journaling practice, which aids in emotional processing and self-reflection.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; persistent irritability noted; sleep quality improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue reported, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/75 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears slightly fatigued but engaged; mood appears anxious with mild distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Recommend ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to further address irritability and concentration challenges. Discuss potential referrals for stress management techniques if symptoms persist. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and melatonin 3 mg nightly; reassess efficacy and side effects in one month. Monitor for any changes in sleep architecture. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. Reassess in one month and consider referral to a neurologist if headaches worsen or if new symptoms develop. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued lifestyle modifications, including regular physical activity and dietary adjustments. Consider referral to a sleep specialist for further evaluation of potential underlying conditions, including sleep apnea or thyroid dysfunction. Discuss work-related stressors and recommend stress management techniques to enhance energy levels.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-04-23 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
